item.title: Containment/termination
item.content:encoded: Building on the former ideas of creating a vacuum to prevent sound from reaching the SCP, why not have the thing be somehow sent to space, and then venting the atmosphere in it? Since there's no gravity, the SCP will have difficulty making contact with any solid surface that could transmit vibrations. Also, if the container was made out of rubber, that would reduce sound created by impact a lot. Finally, in space there is most likely very little rhythmic or melodic sounds, which are supposed to the most beneficial to the SCPs quote.

Seconding this. For such a complex SCP (for want of a better word), it seems there's a lot missing. It should at least give a decent reason for having Keter rating. How this got +73 I'll never guess.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I agree with Fawkes on this one, it needs to be downgraded to Euclid. Unless I missed something, this thing technically passes the locked box test. Stick it in a giant, soundproof box, and don't open it, and nothing will happen that we know of yet. If you want to consider that not knowing what will happen, that still only makes it Euclid. Keter is defined rather well for us newbies as "Stick it in a box and all hell breaks loose", which implies that an SCP requires constant maintenance of some sort in order to prevent a shitstorm; the main point of doing so being that we'd know if we did not perform X, Shitstorm Y would kill us all. We do not know yet if putting in a box and leaving it there for awhile will elicit a response. Euclid is defined as "Stick it in a box not knowing what will happen", which fits this 'angel' rather well.

It's a very minor detail, but I'd think its classification in universe is just as important as anything else in the containment procedures. It sets the tone for the procedures themselves. That said, the rest is lovely. I raised an eyebrow at the neurotoxin part, but that could just be my opinion that a being of this nature wouldn't use pain-inducing means that we as humans are familiar with.
